# Spec — Scene unload and swap: one live scene, an authorable Scene Transition, and a scene-aware Runtime Bridge
<!-- Generated by /sdd-spec on 2026-09-01. Source: issue #66, via grill 2026-08-31-scene-unload-and-swap. State: implemented -->
<!-- SDD-Tracking: version=1; type=spec; state=implemented; issue=#66; grill=2026-08-31-scene-unload-and-swap; superseded-by=none -->

## Context

`loadScene` only ever adds (`packages/engine/src/scene.ts:163-171`): it spawns the JSON's entities, adopts the render and camera blocks and mounts the UI pieces, but removes nothing. The only thing that empties `game.entities` is `dispose()` (`game.ts:265-274`), which also tears down the renderer, input, pointer and UI — a shutdown, not a scene change. Calling `loadScene` twice stacks two scenes: two Players, two Tilemaps, and `dispatchCollisions` (`game.ts:418-452`) pairing entities across both maps. The editor can already author `src/scenes/scene-N.scene.json` (`Editor.tsx:589`), so authoring is ahead of the runtime: you can build a second map and never reach it.

Per-entity teardown is already complete — `Entity.destroy()` cascades `onDestroy` and `Sprite`/`AnimatedSprite`/`Tilemap` dispose geometry, material and textures — so the unload is a scene-level sweep over a primitive that already works. What is missing is the policy: what is scene-scoped and what is session-scoped. That policy is fixed by ADR 0011 and by the `Session-scoped` and `Scene Transition` entries in `CONTEXT.md`, and it is what issues #67 (audio), #74 (camera effects) and #76 (asset loader) explicitly defer to.

## Expected behavior

### Engine — unload and load semantics

- **CA-1** (ALTA): `game.unloadScene()` destroys every scene entity through `Entity.destroy()` — so each component's `onDestroy` runs and GPU resources are released — and leaves `game.entities` empty, spliced in place rather than reassigned (the `Pointer` holds the array by reference, `game.ts:108-113`).
- **CA-2** (ALTA): after `game.unloadScene()` the Game is as newly constructed: `game.registry` is `null`, `game.projection` is `null`, y-sort is off, and `game.view` equals the `viewHeight` the constructor received. `game.stats` and `game.paramOverrides` are unchanged. `spawnPrefab` warns `cannot spawn prefab before loadScene` and returns `null`.
- **CA-3** (ALTA): `loadScene(game, next, registry)` on a Game that already holds a scene replaces it. After the call, exactly one entity named `Player` and one `Tilemap` component exist — no duplicates from the outgoing scene.
- **CA-4** (ALTA): the swap does not touch subscriptions. A handler registered with `game.events.on(...)` and a callback registered with `game.onUpdate(...)` before the swap still fire after it, and fire **exactly once** per event/frame.
- **CA-5** (ALTA): UI scoping. On unload, the pieces named in the outgoing scene's `ui` list are unmounted, and so are pieces shown with `{ scope: 'scene' }`. A piece the host showed without a scope stays mounted and visible. The definition catalog (`GameUi`'s sources) survives, so re-showing a piece after the next load does not need a re-`define`.
- **CA-6** (ALTA): an incoming scene with no `camera` block restores the constructor's `viewHeight`. Loading a scene with a `camera` block after one without it still frames per the block (`setSceneCamera`, `game.ts:195-211`).
- **CA-7** (ALTA): the swap is deferred to the end of the frame. Inside an `onCollide` handler that triggers a transition, `game.entities` still holds the outgoing scene's entities; the incoming scene's entities are present only from the next frame. The load runs after `dispatchCollisions` and `updateSceneCamera` complete.

### Engine — the scene catalog

- **CA-8** (ALTA): the host registers a scene catalog on the Game, and `game.loadSceneByName('<name>')` resolves through it and loads that scene. An unknown name emits a `console.warn` naming the missing scene and leaves the live scene untouched — no unload, no partial state.
- **CA-9** (ALTA): the name of the live scene is readable from the Game and appears in `RuntimeSnapshot` alongside `stats` (`runtime-inspection.ts:53-57`). With no scene loaded the field is `null`.

### Behaviors — `SceneTransition`

- **CA-10** (ALTA): a `SceneTransition` with `trigger: 'overlap'` (the default) fires the swap when the player's `Hitbox` overlaps its own, following the `Collectible`/`Hazard` pattern.
- **CA-11** (ALTA): with `trigger: 'interact'` it fires from the interaction of a sibling `Interactable` on the same entity — it implements no radius and no prompt of its own, so the existing nearest-wins scan (`interactable.ts:55-78`) arbitrates a door and a villager in range. Without that sibling it emits a `console.warn` at ready time and never fires.
- **CA-12** (ALTA): `SceneTransition` is exported from `@waica/behaviors` and registered in the platformer, topdown and isometric registries. The MCP archetype conformance suite passes for all three, and `list_components` reports it with its authoring metadata.

### Archetype and tooling

- **CA-13** (ALTA): the isometric archetype ships two demo scenes. `create_project archetype:isometric start:demo` emits both under `src/scenes/`; `start:blank` still emits only the blank scene. The platformer and topdown archetypes keep exactly one demo scene each.
- **CA-14** (ALTA): `scripts/sync-scene.mjs` propagates both isometric scenes to `examples/isometric/src/scenes/` and to the editor template, and the existing dist byte-equality checks stay green.
- **CA-15** (ALTA): `control_runtime` accepts `operation: 'scene'` with a scene name and loads it in the Run Session; `RUNTIME_BRIDGE_CAPABILITIES` gains `'scene'` with no protocol bump (the `'click'` precedent, `runtime-bridge.ts:9-18`); a session against an engine without the capability gets the existing upgrade message rather than a silent no-op; an unknown scene name returns a structured `runtime-operation-failed` error naming the available scenes.
- **CA-16** (ALTA): `validate_project` emits a warning when a `SceneTransition` names a scene that does not exist in the Project, naming the prefab or entity that carries it.

### Host and browser

- **CA-17** (MEDIA): the four `main.ts` files (three examples plus the editor template, mirrored into the MCP-bundled template) collect every `src/scenes/*.scene.json` and register the catalog on the Game, and each app still boots on `main`. Verified by the app running, not by inspection.
- **CA-18** (MEDIA): in a generated isometric Project driven through the real MCP over stdio in Chrome, walking the player into the transition and crossing it yields a snapshot whose scene name is the destination, whose entities no longer include the outgoing map's, and whose stats still carry a value set before the crossing. A second pass reaches the same scene directly through `control_runtime operation:'scene'`.

### Editor

- **CA-19** (ALTA): changing the open scene loads it over the **same** `Game` instead of remounting. In a mounted `Viewport`, switching the `scene` prop leaves the outgoing scene's entities gone and the incoming scene's present on one `Game` instance whose identity did not change, with selection cleared, the grid overlay, selection gizmo and camera gizmo still attached to the live scene, and the editor's pan/zoom preserved. Rebuilds driven by `epoch` and by `mode` keep recreating the `Game`.

### Game feel

- **CA-20** (NULA — requires human proof): crossing the transition reads as intentional rather than accidental. See the manual protocol in `## Verification plan`.

## Out of scope

- **Additive / streaming scene loading.** The engine holds exactly one live scene; there is no supported way to have two at once.
- **Camera fades and visual transitions (#74), an asset cache that survives the swap (#76), audio policy (#67).** All three consume this decision; none is implemented here.
- **Named entry points or a spawn position declared by the transition.** The incoming scene places its own `Player` wherever that scene authored it, so returning through the same door does not land you beside it.
- **An initial-scene field in `game.json`.** The project format does not change.
- **Routing the editor's `epoch` (structural) or `mode` (edit↔play) rebuilds through `loadScene`.** Only the scene-file change adopts the new API.
- **Asset preloading, a "scene ready" promise, or any asynchrony in loading.** The unload and load are synchronous within the deferred end-of-frame slot.
- **Level-1 authoring of transitions beyond dragging the component in.** No editor UI for picking a destination scene beyond the ordinary prop inspector.

## Inferences

| # | Inference | Chosen | Alternative considered | Confidence | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Where the demo's second scene lives | In the isometric archetype: the manifest exposes a demo scene set, and `sync-scene.mjs`, `create-project.ts` and the editor template emit N scenes | Only in `examples/isometric` — far smaller blast radius, but the e2e leg runs on a **generated** Project (`runtime-e2e.mjs:682`) and `create-project.ts:93,108` writes a single `main.scene.json`, so the leg could not reach it and a new project would not see the two-map demo | alta | confirmed |
| 2 | How the engine learns the live scene's name | The host registers a catalog and `game.loadSceneByName(name)` resolves it, loads it and records the name — one API for both the Scene Transition and the MCP | A fourth `loadScene` parameter, or a `name` field on `SceneJson` (duplicates the filename and forces the editor to write it) | media | confirmed |
| 3 | When the swap is applied within the frame | Deferred to the end of the frame: the transition enqueues and `runFrame` applies the load after `dispatchCollisions` and `updateSceneCamera` | Synchronous inside `onCollide`, relying on the existing `alive` guards — does not crash, but finishes the collision double loop over the outgoing map with the incoming map already in `game.entities` | alta | confirmed |
| 4 | Where the live scene appears in the snapshot | A new field on `RuntimeSnapshot`, beside `stats`: `RuntimeSnapshot extends RuntimeMetadata`, and `stats` already lives there as game state while `RuntimeMetadata` is bridge-owned | On `RuntimeMetadata`, which would also ship it in every `RuntimeControlResult` | alta | confirmed |
| 5 | How the bridge declares the new capability | `RUNTIME_BRIDGE_CAPABILITIES` gains `'scene'`, no protocol bump — the documented pattern for `'click'` | Bump to protocol 2, forcing renegotiation with older engines for no reason | alta | confirmed |
| 6 | The component's name | `SceneTransition`, matching the `CONTEXT.md` term | `Door` / `Portal` / `SceneExit` — more evocative in the editor picker, but the glossary lists exactly those as terms to avoid | media | confirmed |
| 7 | How the trigger mode is declared | Prop `trigger: 'overlap' \| 'interact'`, default `'overlap'` | `onInteract: boolean`, or two separate components | media | confirmed |
| 8 | A transition naming a scene that does not exist | `console.warn` and no-op, plus a `validate_project` warning — the repo's pattern for broken references (`game.ts:135-138`, `scene.ts:129`, `scene.ts:146`) | Throw: loud and early, but breaks the rule that bad scene data never takes down the whole game | alta | confirmed |
| 9 | The shape of scene-scoped UI | `game.ui.show(name, { scope: 'scene' })`, and `loadScene` marks the scene's own `ui` list as scene-scoped automatically | A separate `showForScene(name)` method: more explicit, duplicates `GameUi`'s surface | media | confirmed |

All nine were shown to the user and confirmed as proposed; none was resolved by assumption.

## Verifiability

**Mixed — 17 ALTA · 2 MEDIA · 0 BAJA · 1 NULA.**

The bulk is ALTA because `.sdd/project.md` records `pnpm test` verified green (1214 tests / 133 files, 5.99s, deterministic, no external services), and the whole retention policy is pure observable logic. Integrated boots over the real shipped scene are an established pattern in this repo: `examples/isometric/src/demo-combat.test.ts` runs a real `Game` + `loadScene` under happy-dom with three's `WebGLRenderer` mocked through the engine's own copy.

**CA-19 is ALTA by explicit user choice of mechanism, not by default.** It would have been MEDIA: `packages/editor` has 38 test files and every one of them tests a pure helper — nothing mounts a React component or exercises the `Game` lifecycle, so the only mechanism available today is the contract's ladder step 7 (live editor plus Playwright MCP). The user chose to add editor component-test infrastructure instead. The cost is bounded and measured: the WebGL and `ResizeObserver` recipe already exists and is copyable (`demo-combat.test.ts:1-46`), and mounting the `Viewport` needs **no new dependency** — the editor already depends on `react@^19` and `react-dom@^19`, and React 19 exports `act` from `react` and `createRoot` from `react-dom/client`.

**CA-17 and CA-18 are MEDIA by nature**, not by tooling gaps: they need a real browser. The contract has that gate verified — `pnpm test:e2e`, 16.71s, Google Chrome 151.0.7922.175, and a missing compatible Chrome is a failure, never a skip.

**CA-20 is NULA.** The contract lists game feel explicitly under "Not verifiable without a human".

### Generation policy conflicts

- 🔴 **`max-lineas-archivo` (950) vs `packages/editor/src/editor/Viewport.tsx`, at 1310 lines.** CA-19 requires touching it. The spec's reading: the gate does not cover `.tsx`. The policy row says "cada `.ts` del diff", and its sibling `higiene-ts-diff` globs `packages/*/src/*.ts`; if `.tsx` were covered, `Viewport.tsx` would be permanently frozen and this decision would be unexecutable. **The run must confirm this reading against the actual gate before touching the file, and stop to report if the gate does cover `.tsx`** — do not work around it by splitting `Viewport.tsx`, which is a refactor outside this scope.
- 🟡 **`max-lineas-archivo` vs `packages/mcp/src/validation.ts`, at 904 lines.** CA-16 adds a rule. Mitigation fixed here: the Scene Transition rule goes in a new `packages/mcp/src/scene-transition-validation.ts`, not into `validation.ts`.
- 🟢 `tests-acompañan-src`: engine, behaviors, mcp and editor all add `.ts`/`.tsx` under `src/` and all add tests — satisfied by construction.
- 🟢 `naming-archivos`: `scene-transition.ts`, `scene-transition-validation.ts` (kebab-case `.ts`); `runtime-inspection.test.ts` (kebab-case `.ts`, a new dedicated file — none existed before).
- **[DEVIATION 2026-09-01]** The claim that `Viewport.scene-swap.test.tsx` "matches the allowed `.tsx` form" does not hold against the gate's actual regex: `^(...|([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*|[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*)\.tsx)$` requires the part before `.tsx` to be EITHER a dot-free PascalCase token OR all-kebab-case — a mixed `Viewport.scene-swap.test` basename matches neither (verified empirically: `echo "Viewport.scene-swap.test.tsx" | grep -E '...'` → no match). The run renamed the file to `viewport-scene-swap.test.tsx` (all-kebab-case, verified to match) instead of accepting a POL-naming-archivos FALLA. Scope unchanged — CA-19's mechanism and coverage are identical either way.
- 🟢 `higiene-ts-diff`: nothing here needs `any`, a `@ts-` directive, a default export or an `enum`.
- **No PR-size policy is active** (the generic policies were declined on 2026-08-06), so no partition is proposed despite a large blast radius: engine, behaviors, three archetypes, four hosts, the editor, the MCP, two scripts and the e2e harness. One spec and one PR is grill decision 21.

### CA-17, CA-18 — `pnpm test:e2e` (~17s, real Chrome)

A new leg beside `runIsometricLeg` (`scripts/runtime-e2e.mjs:682`), not folded into it, so a failure is diagnosable on its own: generate an isometric Project through `create_project`, start a Run Session, set a stat, drive the player with semantic input and exact steps until the transition fires, then `inspect` and assert the scene name changed, the outgoing map's entities are gone and the stat survived. Then a second pass reaching a scene directly through `control_runtime operation:'scene'`, plus the negative case of an unknown scene name.

### CA-20 — human protocol

1. Run `pnpm dev:isometric` and open the printed URL.
2. Walk toward the transition from three different angles, including tangentially along its edge.
3. Confirm no tangential approach fires it without intent — if one does, the transition's `Hitbox` is too generous; report the angle.
4. Cross it deliberately and confirm the cut does not disorient: you can tell where you are on the new map within a second.
5. Cross back and confirm that landing at the destination map's authored `Player` position (not beside the door) reads as acceptable, per grill decision 18.

### Full ladder before the PR

`pnpm typecheck` → `pnpm test` → `pnpm build` → `pnpm test:dist` → `pnpm test:e2e`. No CI runs on PRs, so this local ladder is the only pre-merge enforcement.

## Risks and gaps

- **[DEVIATION 2026-09-01] The Door's position in the meadow scene collided with the pre-existing isometric e2e leg twice during implementation, not with anything a CA specified.** First at `[8, 6]` (inside the player's walk-test radius: the northwest movement assertion started reading the cave's fresh Player instead of the meadow's, mid-test). Then at `[13, 13]` (exactly the isometric leg's click-to-move ground-click target). Final position `[2, 2]`, in the meadow's north-west corner, clear of the movement corridor, the click-to-move/orc-click targets and every existing prop; `packages/mcp/src/scene-transition-validation.test.ts` and `examples/isometric/src/demo-scene-swap.test.ts` reference the Door by name, not position, so neither needed a change. Scope unchanged — this is furniture placement for CA-13's demo content, not a criterion.
- **Public surface in lockstep.** `loadScene` changes semantics in `@waica/engine`, which publishes on one version with five other packages. No known consumer of the additive behavior exists (every host calls it once, `setupPlatformer` calls it once), but it is an observable contract change and the PR body must say so.
- **This policy is precedent for three open issues.** ADR 0011 records it; #67, #74 and #76 inherit it rather than re-decide. If the run finds a reason to deviate from the retention line, that is an ADR revision, not a local call.
- **The editor is the most demanding consumer and its test infrastructure is brand new here.** `Viewport.tsx` is 1310 lines with a single `useEffect` spanning lines 370-694 that owns the grid overlay, selection gizmo, multi-selection gizmo pool, camera gizmo, UI preview and the per-frame `onUpdate`. Reloading a scene over the same `Game` must keep all of them attached. This is the highest regression risk in the change, and the reason CA-19 got a real test instead of a smoke.
- **The 950-line gate on `Viewport.tsx` is unresolved until the run checks it** (see the red item under Verifiability). It is the one thing that could block execution on a policy rather than on code. **Resolved 2026-09-01, confirmed before touching the file**: `.sdd/project.md`'s own gate description ("script: `wc -l` sobre cada `.ts` del diff") and `higiene-ts-diff`'s sibling glob (`packages/*/src/*.ts`) both name `.ts` only; no gate script in the repo covers `.tsx`. The spec's reading holds — CA-19 proceeded against `Viewport.tsx` unmodified-by-policy, no split.
- **Deviation from the source handoff, recorded rather than silently reinterpreted.** The handoff assumed "the new e2e leg runs against the real isometric demo, not a synthetic project". The e2e harness actually drives Projects **generated from the archetype** through `create_project`. With inference 1 resolved as "the second scene lives in the archetype", the generated Project carries the real demo and the assumption holds in substance — but the literal wording was wrong and the run should read it that way.
- **`sync-scene.mjs` and `create-project.ts` currently assume one scene per archetype** (`create-project.ts:93,108` writes a single `src/scenes/main.scene.json`). Widening that to a set touches the archetype manifest type, all three archetype packages' manifests, both scaffolding paths and the MCP snapshot tests. It is the largest single mechanical slice of the change.
- **Accidental transitions are game feel** and only CA-20 covers them. If the human protocol fails, the fix is tuning the transition's `Hitbox` in the demo, not changing the trigger semantics.
- **Contract drift, informational**: `.sdd/project.md` records 1214 tests in 133 files (refreshed 2026-08-29); the most recent spec's execution log reports 1285 tests in 140 files after the point-and-click merge. Commands and gates are unchanged, so the verdict is unaffected.

### Code-review round (2026-09-01)

A `/code-review` pass over the PR found three defects, all fixed on the same branch with tests that fail without the fix:

1. **The editor reloaded the whole scene on every edit.** The scene-file effect compared the `scene` prop by object identity, but `ops.*` are pure, so every drag and every prop tweak commits a fresh `SceneJson` — each one read as "another scene was opened", destroying and respawning the entities and clearing the selection mid-drag. The effect is now keyed on the scene's **file path**.
2. **…and it never fired for a real scene switch.** Removing the React key was not enough: `Editor.tsx` still blanked `scene` to `null` while the next file was read, which swapped the `Viewport` for a hint `<div>` and unmounted it, rebuilding the `Game` exactly as before. The loaded scene and its path now travel together in one state, so the previous scene stays mounted (and editable, against its own path) until the next one lands. Without this, CA-19 held only in the isolated component test.
3. **The queued mid-frame swap could be silently overridden.** `loadSceneByName` overwrote an existing `pendingSceneLoad` without a guard, and the out-of-frame branch never cleared one — so two transitions in a frame sent the player to the second door's destination with no signal, and a `control_runtime operation:'scene'` call between frames reported success while the next frame's flush undid it. First-of-frame now wins and warns, an out-of-frame load is authoritative and drops the queue, and `unloadScene()` drops it too.

Also closed in this round: grill decision 8, which the original run left unimplemented because no CA required it — `Interactable` and `click-to-move` now show the prompt with `{ scope: 'scene' }`, so it dies with its scene instead of surviving into a map where nothing hides it. And the editor now registers the scene catalog before loading, so crossing a `SceneTransition` in Play resolves instead of logging `unknown scene`.

**Pre-existing, noted and not touched** (per the standing rule that this change only fixes what it introduced): `packages/mcp/src/runtime-dev-server.ts:62-66` tolerates only `ESRCH` when signalling a process group, so under parallel test load an already-reaped group leader surfaces as `kill EPERM` and fails `runtime-dev-server.test.ts`. Observed once in a full-suite run, green on the immediate re-run and green in isolation. Worth its own issue.

### Second code-review round (2026-09-01)

A second `/code-review` pass confirmed the three defects above were closed with tests that fail without the fix, and found two more — one of them opened by the first round's own fix:

4. **The scene-switch window was unguarded.** Keeping the previous scene mounted while the next file reads (fix 2 above) created a window where `openScenePath` names the incoming file but the screen, and `commit`, still belong to the outgoing one. Two concrete failures: an edit made in that window was written into the file the user had just navigated away from while the breadcrumb, title and scene picker all named the other one; and pressing Play in that window built the run from the outgoing scene under the incoming one's name, after which the arriving read hot-swapped the scene under the live session, since the `[scenePath]` effect is keyed on the path and not on the mode. Both mutation entry points for the displayed scene — `commit` and `play()` — now refuse to act while `sceneSwitching` holds. Deletion and undo/redo were already safe: they take an explicit path rather than the displayed scene.
5. **`GameUi.show` could promote a session-scoped piece to scene-scoped.** `if (options.scope) piece.scope = options.scope` set the scope on every call, so a scene whose own `ui` list happened to name a piece the host had already mounted took ownership of it, and the next unload destroyed a HUD meant to outlive the map — directly against CA-5's "a piece the host showed without a scope stays mounted and visible". Scope is now decided by whoever mounts the piece and no later `show` changes it, in either direction.

**Coverage gap, stated rather than papered over**: finding 4's guard has no automated test. Reaching it means mounting `Editor.tsx` and driving its async `openScenePath`/`openScene` race, and the editor has no component-test path for that component — it pulls Monaco, which happy-dom cannot host. What bounds the risk is that the guard surface is exactly two functions: every mutation of the displayed scene goes through `commit`, and every run through `play()`. Finding 5 is covered by two new `ui.test.ts` cases, one per direction.

### Scope addition beyond CA-16 (2026-09-02): `SceneTransition.trigger:'interact'` needs a sibling `Interactable`

Not required by CA-16 as written — CA-16 only covers a `SceneTransition` naming an unknown scene. This is a second, related static check the same validator did not yet have: `SceneTransition`'s own runtime contract (`packages/behaviors/src/scene-transition.ts:30-37`) requires a sibling `Interactable` when `trigger:'interact'`, or the component never fires. Before this addition that gap was only ever caught by a `console.warn` in `onReady` — a door misauthored this way passed `validate_project` clean and stayed silently dead. Requested and implemented as an explicit scope extension of this already-implemented spec, not a new issue.

**Files touched**: `packages/mcp/src/scene-transition-validation.ts` (rule), `packages/mcp/src/scene-transition-validation.test.ts` (unit + one full-pipeline test), `packages/mcp/src/validation.ts` (new `FindingCode` member, `validateEntitySceneTransition` call site now threads `prefabs`), `packages/mcp/src/validation.test.ts` (isometric-demo-stays-clean assertion for the new code).

**New finding**: severity `warning`, code `scene-transition-missing-interactable`, message `SceneTransition on "<carrier>" has trigger:"interact" but no sibling Interactable; it will never fire.` — deliberately close to the `onReady` warning's wording. `ref` is the carrying entity/prefab ref (matching `checkComponent`'s `unknown-component` convention for findings with no external target).

**Design points carried from the brief**:
- The effective `trigger` is resolved through the same three layers as everywhere else in this file: a scene-level `overrides.SceneTransition.trigger` wins over the component's own prop, and the default with neither present is `'overlap'`.
- The sibling-`Interactable` check looks at the entity's *effective* component set — the resolved prefab's components plus the entity's inline ones — so a prefab-supplied `Interactable` clears an inline `trigger:'interact'` `SceneTransition` (the trap case the brief called out), and vice versa. `validateEntitySceneTransition` gained a `prefabs: ReadonlyMap<string, PrefabJson>` parameter for this (mirroring the pattern `validateScene` already receives it from `validateProject`'s per-project prefab map).
- No duplicate finding: a plain prefab instance with no override touching `trigger` is left entirely to `validatePrefabSceneTransition` (same discipline the existing unknown-target check already followed); the entity-level check only fires for an inline `SceneTransition` or a `trigger`-touching override.
- Order of components in the JSON is irrelevant — this is static validation over parsed JSON, unlike the runtime `onReady` scan.

**Tests added** — `scene-transition-validation.test.ts`, describe block `validatePrefabSceneTransition (interact needs a sibling Interactable)`:
- `is silent when a trigger:"interact" SceneTransition has a sibling Interactable` — prefab, clean case.
- `warns when a trigger:"interact" SceneTransition has no sibling Interactable` — prefab, warning case.

describe block `validateEntitySceneTransition (interact needs a sibling Interactable)`:
- `is silent for an inline trigger:"interact" SceneTransition when the prefab supplies the Interactable` — the false-positive trap.
- `warns for a trigger override to "interact" over a prefab with no Interactable` — override case.
- `is silent when trigger is absent (default "overlap") even without a sibling Interactable` — default-trigger case.

Plus one full-pipeline case in the new `validateProject (interact needs a sibling Interactable, full pipeline)` describe block — `threads the real prefab map into the entity-level Interactable check` — a two-entity scene (`Door`: inline interact trigger, prefab-supplied `Interactable`, clean; `Gate`: override to interact over a prefab with no `Interactable`, warns) run through the real `validateProject`/`makeProject` pipeline, proving the `prefabs` argument threads correctly from files on disk, not just from a literal test `Map`. All six cases were verified to fail against the pre-fix code (confirmed by temporarily reverting `scene-transition-validation.ts` to its prior committed version and re-running the suite) before being restored.

`validation.test.ts`'s existing isometric-demo test (`reports no unknown-scene-transition-target for the generated isometric demo`) gained one more assertion: zero `scene-transition-missing-interactable` findings. Confirmed by inspection first — neither shipped Door prefab (`examples/isometric/src/objects/door.object.json`, `packages/archetype-isometric/src/prefabs.ts:251`) sets `trigger`, so both stay on the default `'overlap'` and the new rule never fires on the demo.

**Deviation from the literal brief, and why**: the brief's plumbing note pointed at `validation.test.ts` for "whatever the plumbing touch needs." Landing all three original end-to-end cases there (isometric-demo assertion + three full `validateProject` tests) pushed `validation.test.ts` from 914 to 1013 lines — over the 950-line `max-lineas-archivo` ratchet, and a regression this change would have introduced (the file was under the cap before touching it). Consolidated the three full-pipeline tests into one two-entity case and moved it into `scene-transition-validation.test.ts` instead (which already imports nothing from `validation.test.ts` and had ample headroom), keeping only the small isometric-demo assertion in `validation.test.ts` (921 lines final). The unit-level coverage in `scene-transition-validation.test.ts` already exercises the exact `prefabs` plumbing with real `Map` instances; the relocated full-pipeline test adds the one thing those didn't — prefab resolution from real files on disk — without breaking the ratchet.

**Explicitly not touched, flagged instead** (per the standing rule — this change fixes only what it introduces): the runtime `onReady` check in `packages/behaviors/src/scene-transition.ts:31` has an order bug — it warns a false positive when `SceneTransition` appears before `Interactable` in the entity's component array, because `Entity.has` at `onReady` time can only see components constructed so far. Out of scope for this addition; worth its own fix.
